correctness.rationale: For every omitted crown vertex the identifying set is the selected opposite part minus the matched endpoint. Ordered differences give the solid omission rule; domination removes exactly two one-index boundary families. The self criterion against codewords forces two-sided omissions to have equal index sets, after which solidness leaves only one matched pair. Direct exhaustive testing through n=8 confirms all coefficients and minimum counts.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural and enumerative theorem for two established stronger locating-domination notions on a canonical dense bipartite family. It determines every feasible code, both cardinality polynomials, both minima, and both basis counts, while exposing a sharp change caused by deleting one perfect matching from a complete bipartite graph.
